note: no para nums (text near end): challenge to Criminal Law (Amendment) Act 1969 s.6 amending CPC s.7 to let magistrates sentence under s.296 rejected: "We can see no valid ground for assuming that the said amendment was contrary to the Constitution of Kenya"

para 27 (Mwera JA, one of 6 separate rulings; also headnote holding 4): "section 75 of the Civil Procedure Act ... [should not] be read to mean that these provisions of law also confer the right of appeal"; borderline obiter, main issue is Arbitration Act s.35

paras 22-24: HC substituted sentence; CA reinstates death sentence applying Mwaura: "the High Court misguided itself in substituting the death sentence" - a sentence set aside, not an event on s.296; no earlier event reversed
para 26: converts life to 30 yrs "in light of the emerging jurisprudence" (Maingi, Kitsao para 25); no own reasoned holding on s.8(2), just sentence adjustment

paras 19-21: relies on A.W.M and A.O.O ("held that section 25(2) ... is inconsistent"): "jurisprudence ... is now well settled, and we will not pretend to reinvent the wheel"; quote is about the sentence not a declaration

paras 27-28: no independent adjudication; defers to SC Muruatetu directions: "not, at this jurisprudential moment, and by dint of the Supreme Court's directions, unconstitutional"; issue "yet to be addressed"

para 10: "we declare that the mandatory nature of the sentence of life imprisonment ... by dint of section 8(2) ... is unconstitutional" (own declaration, though reasons rest on CA Mwangi/Manyeso paras 7-9)
para 25: "we declare that the mandatory nature of the sentence of life imprisonment ... section 8(2) ... is unconstitutional" (reasons borrowed from Mwangi/Manyeso/Ayako paras 22-24)

paras 38-40: rejects challenge solely by applying SC Muruatetu directions and Simiyu: "its applicability to defilement cases ... dealt a deathblow by the Supreme Court"; no own constitutional reasoning
paras 10-11: applies SC Mwangi clarification: "The implications of this clarification directly dispose the present appeal"; no own holding on s.296(2)

paras 48-51: construes "aged eleven years or less" in s.8(2): "a child aged 11 years as contemplated under Section 8 (2) ... will only be 12 years a day preceding his twelfth birth day"; the quoted sentence is the application to the appellant, not the interpretive holding
para 153 (and 141-142): "we find sections 22 and 23 of the Act unconstitutional"; "the Act" = Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act 2018, NOT KICA (KICA never mentioned)

para 101: "Section 5, as drafted, is therefore harmless and constitutional" (though mainly held challenge speculative/premature); Act is Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act s.5 (Committee composition), not KICA; whole s.5 composition was at issue so total not partial
paras 146-147: s.24(1)(c) "the limitation is reasonable, proportional and justifiable"; section is Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act s.24 (child pornography), not KICA s.24
para 150: "We thus find that the section is constitutionally sound"; section is Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act s.27 (cyber harassment), not KICA s.27
para 151: "we reject the appellant's challenge to section 28 of the Act"; section is Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act s.28 (cybersquatting), not KICA s.28

para 131: "our understanding of that provision is that the word "shall" is used in relation to the possible orders that a court can issue"; provision is Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act s.50(2) (production orders), not KICA s.50

para 132: challenge to six-month real-time traffic data collection rejected, "does not of itself render the provision unconstitutional"; provision is Computer Misuse and Cybercrimes Act s.52, not KICA; ruling only on the duration aspect so partial not total
"ISSUES" part (unnumbered): "we do declare sub-section 17 [2] of the Act, unconstitutional and, thus, void"; "the Act" = Trade Disputes Act (Cap 234), NOT Civil Procedure Act

no para nums: s.123(2) CPC bar on bail for capital offences void under Art 2(4)/49(1)(h): "S. 123(2) cannot be used as a basis to deny any suspect bail"; no formal declaration but own reasoned holding of inconsistency (arguably read_down)
para 27 "section 45(3) declared invalid to the extent of its inconsistency"; final order para 34(c) "declaring section 45(3) of the Employment Act 2007 invalid"

para 49: "the provisions of section 38 and 40 of the Civil Procedure Act ... are consistent with the Bill of Rights"; only the arrest-and-committal limb of s.38 and its proviso were challenged (paras 35, 44-46), so partial not total
para 49: "the provisions of section 38 and 40 of the Civil Procedure Act ... are consistent with the Bill of Rights"; para 38 construes s.40 as consequent on s.38 procedure
para 74 order (a): "A declaration is hereby issued that Section 84D of KICA is unconstitutional and invalid"

para 162(a): "sections 158, 159 & 160 of the Penal Code are not inconsistent with articles 1, 2, 4 ... of the Constitution"; note conflicting order (j) that they "fail to capture the letter and spirit to the exceptions in article 26(4)"
para 162(a): "sections 158, 159 & 160 of the Penal Code are not inconsistent with ... the Constitution"; order (j) partly undercuts this

paras 42-43: applies CA construction of "is liable" to s.275 itself: "That provision, however, does not impose a mandatory minimum sentence"; "the sentence ... arose from a misconstruing of the provisions of section 275 as imposing a mandatory sentence"
para 180(b): "section 21(2) of the Criminal Procedure Code must be read to permit the use of firearms, if need be, and only in the circumstances construed in paragraphs 1(a) and 1(b)"
para 105: "section 26 of the Sexual Offences Act is constitutional and does not violate or limit the rights of persons living with HIV"; petition dismissed para 109

para 19: adopts Njoroge Mungai but construes s.7 itself to reject defective-charge ground: "In section 7 offence, the person with mental disability is the spectator while in section 146 offence ... is the victim"; borderline (reiterates another court's finding)

para 4: "To that extent that the Sexual Offences Act prescribes a minimum mandatory sentence with no discretion ... fall foul of Article 28" then resentences to 40 yrs (para 9); borderline - words track Maingi's order, little own reasoning, no formal declaration

para 77: declines s.166(2)-(7) committal "alive to the fact that this court has through several rulings found this provision as unconstitutional"; "I am in agreement with Mativo, J ... A.O.O" - follows earlier rulings, no own holding

paras 22-24: petition dismissed for not meeting SC Mwangi threshold ("having not met that threshold required for a finding of the unconstitutionality"), no merits ruling; petitioner was convicted in 2003 under Penal Code s.145(1) (para 1), not SOA s.8
paras 77-78: "Guided by the above decision [Akhonya CA]" translates life to 30 years; no own holding on s.20(1); para 76 even calls it a mandatory life sentence
paras 4-5: applies SC Mwangi "that the mandatory minimum penalties ... are lawful and not unconstitutional"; 1-line revision ruling, no own adjudication

para 22: "These decisions are binding on the High Court ... the proper course ... is to take it that life sentence is unconstitutional" - applies CA Ayako/Manyeso, no own holding; order para 30 substitutes 30 yrs

para 12: court "is unable to declare it unconstitutional" for want of full argument per SC Mwangi; no merits ruling on validity, just declines petition (para 13 "sentence ... is upheld" refers to the sentence)

para 14: "section 46 of the Kenya Broadcasting Corporation Act is in violation of Article 48 ... unconstitutional to that extent"; section is KBC Act s.46, NOT Civil Procedure Act s.3A (only cited as basis of the motion)
